top_choice_rationale: The magic-wavelength lattice is a simple, general mechanism (the light shifts of the two clock levels are made equal by tuning one parameter) that is understood and not merely observed. It makes interrogation of very many neutral atoms possible, which moved stability to the 10^-18 level and opened many-body clock physics. Independent laboratories reproduce it, and the allocation to Katori (idea and first demonstrations) and Ye (accuracy and many-body programme) is clean. A citation naming magic-wavelength trapping keeps it distinct from the 2005 comb and 2012 ion-control prizes, so awarding it is clearly preferable to no award.
